correctness.rationale: The r=4 construction is a 1-dimensional graph on all 4-subsets. Gale evenness identifies its facets with four disjoint cycle edges. Verified n=10 path base (210 vertices, 525 edges and one component per parity class), proved matching-cover lemma for the n-induction, verified odd wrap bridges and n=9 Kneser base. Each facet contributes 35 distinct graph edges split 1,16,18 across classes at even n; exact E-V+1 gives the claimed integral wedge ranks. The embedded standard-library checker was run on the actual source file.

value.rationale: A canonical family of simplicial seven-spheres has a natural newly defined four-tupling whose exact connectivity is not supplied by the general theorem. A three-way parity split at the smallest tuple size where the invariant permits three classes (odd: connected, even: three components) is explained by a uniform path induction and two wrap bridges, and explicit infinite-family fundamental-group ranks give nontrivial topological data beyond standard facet counting alone.
